messages:
mira: noticing p99 jump after kernel-selector roll to fused-attn-v2 on rtx-a100 pool. microbatch fixed=8, p50 unchanged, but p99 from ~1.1s -> ~1.7s for long-chat workloads. KV-cache hitrate also dropped.

sam: can you paste the profiling output and the kv hit rates? did the kernel change touch kv layout? @kevin

mira: profiling snippet (canary run vs baseline):
```
baseline (fused-attn-v1): p50=120ms p95=340ms p99=1100ms kv_hitrate=0.93
canary  (fused-attn-v2): p50=125ms p95=410ms p99=1700ms kv_hitrate=0.60
notes: spike mostly on seq_len>4096, requests that hit cache previously now recompute.
```
I also switched kernel selection to prefer 'pack+fused' path which changes padding/alignment.

dave: ugh. sounds like cache invalidation + large seqs are thrashing. two levers: reduce target_utilization to keep headroom, or make microbatching more conservative for long-context requests. tradeoff = throughput vs tail.

kevin: ran a quick sim of an admission-control tweak. sample config I tested:
```
admission_control:
  target_utilization: 0.72
  max_microbatch: 16
  min_microbatch: 1
  dynamic_scaling: true
  shedding_policy: tail_priority
  seq_len_bucket_thresholds: [512,2048,4096]
```
Result: p99 -> 1.15s (from 1.7), throughput -6% on steady state, but much fewer SLA misses for p99.

deploy-bot: deploy event: kernel-selector v2 -> rtx-a100 pool (canary subset). deploy_id=deploy_2025_11_03_1724

sam: important question — is fused-attn-v2 producing a different KV key encoding (padding/truncation) so cached KV tensor shapes differ? if so, cache misses are expected. we should avoid format churn in a patch release.

mira: correct — v2 uses 128-byte alignment which changes padded length stratification; cache keys include padded_length right now. that made many previously identical requests map to different keys. proposal: add a compatibility mode that normalizes to logical seq_len before keying.

dave: also consider pad-trim during preprocessing: remove trailing padding before cache key calc and store compacted k/v with original positions. cheaper than changing kernels if we can do it in runtime.

kevin: i can run a canary with three changes: (1) pad-trim + normalize keys, (2) dynamic microbatch based on seq_len buckets, (3) admission target=0.72 + tail shedding. projected: p50 ~ same, p95 ~ drop 10-15%, p99 ~ 1.1s, throughput -4..-8%.

mira: thanks — please run that canary and share dashboards. if canary p99 <=1.2s and kv_hitrate >0.85 we keep. otherwise revert selector. tagging as P1 for release rollback if global p99>1.5s. :grimacing:

sam: also add an experiment metric: kv_invalidation_rate by model+kernel_variant (histogram) so we can detect these format regressions automatically.

kevin: will add metric + smoke test. scheduling canary now.

mira: great. quick sync 10m after canary stabilizes. thx all :thumbsup:
